text:
The snapshot looks like early 2013. Unemployment is 7.9%, which matches January or February 2013. The fed funds rate is about 0.14% and the 10-year yield is 1.91%. Gold fell 5% in the month, which fits February 2013, and its 12-month drawdown is about 11.9%. Large-cap equities are up 8.8% over 3 months.

Headline CPI at 1.58% year over year fits February 2013 (it was 2.0% in January and 1.5% in February). The 10-year yield ended February 2013 near 1.88%. Unemployment was 7.7% in February, but 7.9% was the January figure, which was still the latest published at some points. The data may also be vintage-based. The 12-month unemployment change of -0.4 is consistent with 8.3% in February 2012 versus 7.9%.

Large-cap equity returned +0.6% in February 2013, which fits. Developed ex-US was -1.6% and emerging markets -2.6%, which also fits February. Payrolls averaging 200k fits as well.

So the best estimate is February 2013.
